text:
sam: Quick help — PR #4023 adds TF to grant our batch-job SA in acct B permission to decrypt with /alias/data-key. Need a quick sanity check on the key policy + IRSA annotation.

maria: can you paste the tf snippet?

sam: sure
```hcl
resource "aws_kms_key" "data_key" {
  description = "Data key for analytics"
  policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.kms_policy.json
}

resource "aws_iam_role" "batch_sa" {
  name = "batch-job-sa"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.irsa_assume.json
}

resource "aws_kms_grant" "batch_decrypt" {
  key_id = aws_kms_key.data_key.id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.batch_sa.arn
  operations = ["Decrypt"]
}
```

sam: TF plan shows the grant being created but pods still get AccessDenied when calling KMS.

jin: two quick things: 1) grantee_principal for aws_kms_grant must be the IAM role ARN used in STS (for IRSA it's the role assumed), that's correct. 2) pod needs annotation `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/batch-job-sa` and the OIDC provider must be configured for that account.

maria: also double-check the key policy — if the key policy doesn't allow your account or specific principals, grants may be ignored. can you paste the key policy?

sam: pasted snippet
```json
{
 "Version":"2012-10-17",
 "Statement":[
  {"Sid":"Enable IAM","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::111122223333:root"},"Action":"kms:*","Resource":"*"},
  {"Sid":"AllowDecrypt","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::222233334444:role/BatchRole"},"Action":["kms:Decrypt","kms:DescribeKey"],"Resource":"*"}
 ]
}
```

alex: that second principal looks wrong — it points to a role in a different account. For IRSA the principal should be the role ARN in the account where the pod assumes the role (or explicitly allow the account). also avoid using `root` if you can scope tighter.

ops-bot: terraform plan finished with warnings: `aws_kms_grant` can be incompatible with key policy updates in the same apply — consider creating the grant after key policy changes (use depends_on or separate apply).

jin: for cross-account access the recommended flow is: 1) update key policy to allow the target account or specific role 2) create kms_grant for the role ARN (or rely on key policy principals) 3) ensure IRSA OIDC & role mapping are correct. if you rely on session tags/conditions also confirm `kms:ViaService` usage.

sam: quick q — can we reference a KMS alias in external-secrets/helm values instead of the key id?

maria: yes — either pass `alias/my-app-data` to the external-secrets config or resolve `${aws_kms_alias.data_key.target_key_id}` in TF and populate the helm values. many charts accept `kmsKeyId: alias/xxx`.

chris: small gotcha — when EKS pods assume roles via IRSA, calls to KMS are evaluated with the STS caller ARN (assumed-role/session). KMS grants expect the principal ARN of the role (not the session ARN), but AWS handles mapping in most cases. still verify the principal in the grant matches the role ARN.

sam: should I add `depends_on = [aws_kms_key.data_key, aws_iam_role.batch_sa]` to the grant resource to force ordering?

jin: yes, add depends_on to be explicit. and consider `lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }` if you're rotating alias/key. also run plan/apply in two steps if you change the key policy and then add grants.

maria: can someone approve the PR after the depends_on + policy fix? I'll wait for one more review.

alex: I'll take it — doing a local `aws sts assume-role` test to simulate the pod.

ops-bot: test-run: `kubectl apply -f job.yaml` -> pod logs show `AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::111122223333:assumed-role/batch-job-sa/xxxxx is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt` — suggests key policy still doesn't allow that role.

sam: I'll update the PR with an account-scoped principal and add depends_on now. thanks all :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: CI: terraform plan OK after changes (no drift) :white_check_mark:

alex: approved
